name: Town Center (Victoria Park and Racecourse)
tagline: Little England at its most walkable
description: The compact heart of Nuwara Eliya, wrapped around Victoria Park, the old racecourse, the market and the colonial post office. Guesthouses, hotels, cafes and shops sit within easy walking distance, giving the best balance of convenience, atmosphere and colonial character for a stay in town.
bestFor: First-time visitors and those wanting everything walkable
cons: Busy and can feel crowded in season

name: Gregory Lake Area
tagline: Lakeside calm just south of the centre
description: The area around Gregory Lake, a short ride south of the town centre, offers waterfront walks, boat rides, green space and a more relaxed feel. Several guesthouses and hotels sit nearby, making it a scenic, slightly quieter base while staying close to the action.
bestFor: Slower stays wanting lake views and green space
cons: Fewer dining options right at hand

name: Tea Estate Outskirts (toward Pedro and Mackwoods)
tagline: Sleep among the emerald tea fields
description: The plantation fringes toward the Pedro and Mackwoods estates trade town convenience for sweeping tea-country views and quiet. Boutique bungalows and estate guesthouses here put you among rolling green hills and mist, ideal for photographers and walkers who want scenery over nightlife.
bestFor: Photographers, walkers and those seeking quiet and views
cons: Need a tuktuk or driver for town

name: Nanu Oya (the train station side)
tagline: Your gateway to the scenic hill-country train
description: About 8km from Nuwara Eliya, Nanu Oya is the nearest railway station on the famous hill-country line between Kandy, Ella and Badulla. A handful of guesthouses cluster here, handy for rail travellers arriving or departing on the scenic tea-field route.
bestFor: Rail travellers arriving or leaving by the scenic train
pros: On the scenic hill-country rail line
Easy onward travel to Ella and Kandy
